messages:
sam (auditor): Hey team — for SOC2 evidence we need a small reproducible sample: 3 privileged session playbacks (SSH/TACACS) from last quarter + proof of integrity that ties playback to a user identity and KMS key. Also want the retention policy that governed those recordings. Can you provide a sample export and short instructions to verify?

maya (sec-eng): Yep — we can pull that. Which hosts/time window do you want? and do you want raw recordings + redacted transcript or just transcript?

sam (auditor): Raw recordings + redacted transcript preferred. Window: any 3 distinct users between 2025-10-01 and 2025-12-31. Need KMS key id/alias, manifest with checksums, and chain-of-custody notes.

alex (infra): Quick recap of how we record: sessions are proxied through the PSA bastion service -> session metadata written to dynamo table `psa_sessions` -> recordings stored in s3 `s3://redwood-psa-recordings/` encrypted with KMS key alias `alias/redwood/psa` (multi-region CMK). Manifest file (JSON) created per export and encrypted with same CMK.

alex (infra): To pull a sample manifest and a recording we use:```bash
aws s3 cp s3://redwood-psa-recordings/exports/2025Q4/sample-manifest-2025Q4.json.gz ./
gunzip sample-manifest-2025Q4.json.gz
# manifest contains recording keys + sha256 checksums + kms_key_id
aws s3 cp s3://redwood-psa-recordings/$(jq -r .recordings[0].s3_key sample-manifest-2025Q4.json) ./recording1.enc
# decrypt envelope via KMS on our infra side when exporting for auditors
```

maya (sec-eng): I pulled three candidate sessions: user ids alice, ben, carlos from 2025-11-03, 2025-10-21, 2025-12-09. I uploaded a redacted playback bundle to the audit bucket and created an export bundle: `s3://redwood-audit-exports/3109801234/psa-playback-sample-2025Q4.zip`

maya (sec-eng): evidence-bot just created the export and posted manifest:
`evidence-bot: export-id=exp-3109801234, manifest=s3://redwood-audit-exports/3109801234/manifest.json, manifest_sha256=2f9c7b3a1d4f8e5a6b7c9d1f0a2b3c4d5e6f7a8b9c0d1e2f3a4b5c6d7e8f9a0b`

irene (compliance): Retention policy: PSA recordings retention = 180 days by default (config: `infra/config/retention.tf` TTL = 15552000 seconds). We keep manifest records in Dynamo for 365 days for audit mapping. Exports to the audit bucket are immutable (object lock) for the retention window when exported for auditors.

maya (sec-eng): For integrity verification: manifest includes per-file sha256 and kms_key_id. Steps we provide auditors: 1) download recording bundle, 2) compute sha256sum, 3) compare to manifest, 4) verify manifest signature via KMS: we sign manifest with CMK using KMS Sign and include signature blob in the manifest. Example verification:```bash
aws s3 cp s3://redwood-audit-exports/3109801234/manifest.json ./manifest.json
echo -n "$(jq -c .recordings manifest.json)" > payload.bin
# use AWS KMS Verify (auditors with encrypt/verify access or we can provide verification output)
aws kms verify --key-id alias/redwood/psa --message-type RAW --message fileb://payload.bin --signature fileb://manifest.sig --signing-algorithm RSASSA_PSS_SHA_256
```

sam (auditor): Good. Two follow-ups: (1) need the key ID and IAM policy that controls access to `alias/redwood/psa` (2) need notes on redaction process (how we remove PII before giving transcripts).

alex (infra): Key id: `arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:111122223333:key/abcd1234-ef56-7890-ab12-34567890cdef` (we'll include in export README). IAM: only `psa-service-role`, `evidence-export-role`, and `security:audit` principal have Decrypt/Sign permissions. We'll add the IAM policy snippet to the export.

maya (sec-eng): Redaction: we run transcripts through our redaction pipeline (lambda) that replaces email/credit-card/ssn patterns and hashes usernames when requested. Redaction config entry included in export: `redact_config.yaml` and sample redaction log showing applied regex matches for each transcript. We retain a mapping in the secure vault only if the auditor has an approved NDA and key escrow request — otherwise mappings are not exported.

alex (infra): Terraform snippet for TTL on the dynamo table to show retention:```hcl
resource "aws_dynamodb_table" "psa_sessions" {
  name = "psa_sessions"
  ttl {
    attribute_name = "expires_at"
    enabled = true
  }
}
# S3 lifecycle rule on recordings bucket keeps objects 180 days then transitions to GLACIER
```

maya (sec-eng): I will assemble the full export package: - 3 encrypted recordings (decrypted for playback by us, exported as encrypted with audit CMK) - manifest.json + manifest.sig - redact_config.yaml + redaction logs - iam_policy_snippet.txt - readme.md with verification steps and CMK ARN - chain_of_custody.md (who pulled, when, with ticket ids)

maya (sec-eng): ETA: I can deliver the export package and verification README by EOD tomorrow.

sam (auditor): Perfect. Also please add a short vuln note — the 2025-12-09 session touched an instance that had a triaged kernel vuln (CVE-2025-9999) — we need confirmation that the session content was not used to exploit anything and any follow-up.

maya (sec-eng): Noted. I'll include triage note: timeline + remediation state (patch applied 2026-01-02) + whether any suspicious commands were observed (none so far in quick grep).

evidence-bot: export ready: s3://redwood-audit-exports/3109801234/psa-playback-sample-2025Q4.zip (size=42MB)

sam (auditor): Thanks all. I'll review the package once you drop it. Appreciate the quick turnaround.

irene (compliance): tagging for record: #soc2 #iso27001 #psa-evidence
